name: Winnemeg, at the gathering of August 1812
head: winnemeg
review_note: review_required: a Potawatomi person of the gathering at Chicago in August 1812, the eve of the battle in which the garrison and its families were attacked. The card states only what the named sources say, says where a story is Kinzie family tradition rather than a contemporary account, and stages no speech or ceremony.

present_on_scene_date.note: Each person's own card says how their presence on 14 August is known.

associated_with.note: No source places his lodge in the camp; the card is put at one of the camp's grounds on the creek (the 1812 camp records) so it can be found, a reconstructed choice (liberty L-1812-people-3461).

not_in_this_household.note: No source names his family or places his lodge in the camp.

persons.name: Winnemeg

present_on_scene_date.note: Arrived 7, 8 or 9 Aug with the order (sources differ); Wau-Bun (Mrs Helm, hearsay) places him on the field on the 15th. No source names him on the 14th. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Chief; courier who carried Hull's evacuation order to Heald. Potawatomi, St Joseph River (Andreas p. 79).  Afterwards: Not established from sources read here.

evidence.quote: This Letter was brot by a Potowautemie Chief Winnemeg & he informed Capt. Heald through Kenzie to evacuate immediately
evidence.claim: Brought the letter; advised immediate evacuation
evidence.tier: contemporary (written 1812-1815 by a participant or from participants)

evidence.quote: The next day the Indian runner. Winnemac, delivered to Captain Heald at Fort Dearborn his order for the evacuation.
evidence.tier: secondary history (1884-1913), cite as compiler's statement

evidence.quote: On the afternoon of the 7th of August, Winnemeg, or _Catfish_, a Pottowattamie chief, arrived at the post, bringing despatches from General Hull.
evidence.claim: Wau-Bun dates his arrival 7 Aug and glosses the name
evidence.tier: Kinzie family tradition (Wau-Bun; pamphlet 1836/1844, book 1856; Quaife App. II judges its speeches and dialogue invented)

evidence.quote: he was met by _Winnemeg_ and _Wau-ban-see_, who endeavored to save him from the savages who had now overtaken him.
evidence.claim: 15 Aug, with Waubansee, at Wells's death (Mrs Helm's story)
evidence.tier: Kinzie family tradition (Wau-Bun; pamphlet 1836/1844, book 1856; Quaife App. II judges its speeches and dialogue invented)

evidence.quote: Topenebe and Winnemeg were on the St. Joseph River.

evidence.quote: through the influence of Winnemeg, the Pottawatomies did not join.
